documents.title: GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery
documents.summary: GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery Here's an interesting case-study in using GPT-6.2 Astra for historical research, from history professor Mark Humphries: With only minimal prompting, GPT-6.2 Astra was able to autonomously identify the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook held at Yale’s Beinecke Library . It did so extremely quickly (in just 22 minutes), using publicly available primary and secondary sources. To do so, it discovered a little known source in a paper archive, predicted that it would prove its hypothesis if examined and, in the end, it did. Not only that, but this new source turns out to be a major find on its own that will be of significant interest to both Canadian and fur trade historians. Here's the digitized sketchbook . Astra found a diary reference reference to a visit by the vicomte de Chabot dated five days before a date mentioned in the sketchbook at a nearby river, and suggested that Chabot's journal of his travels (only available by order from Cleveland State University) might confirm that the sketchbook was his work. documents.title: datasette-charts 0.2a0
documents.summary: Release: datasette-charts 0.2a0 I introduced this new charting plugin for Datasette yesterday . Today it's gained integration with Datasette Agent , so now you can ask chat for a chart and it will create one for you using the same underlying chart suggestion and generation tools. Here's a demo video, recorded on agent.datasette.io where you can sign in with GitHub to try the plugin yourself: Download the video (MP4) I prompt Datasette Agent to "Use #stats to show sqlite-utils downloads over time as a chart" - where typing "#stats" opens a table search box. It shows me a chart inline in the chat, and when I click "Open in the chart builder" it opens the chart in a panel along with the table page. I use the table page to switch to a chart of "datasette", then when I ask the agent "what does the chart show?" it notices that I changed the content in the panel and describes the new Datasette chart to me. Here's a Markdown export of the chat from the video. Tags: datasette-agent , datasette , visualization
